summary: Full E2E testing of the Pedidos (Purchase Orders) module - backend + frontend. 16/16 pytest backend tests passed (auth allowlist, catalog CRUD, order CRUD, status workflow, PDF, sequential numbering, custom item auto-save). Frontend Playwright walked the complete flow: login as leonicelaboratorio@lumix.com (Laboratorio mode) -> nav-pedidos visible -> /pedidos page renders with fazer-pedido-button and both tabs -> open dialog -> select real supplier -> add custom item via '+ adicionar item novo' -> item appears in catalog -> add to cart with qty -> edit cart qty -> observations -> Finalize -> order PED-0007 appears in Histórico -> status workflow pendente -> enviado -> recebido -> reabrir all work -> PDF endpoint returns HTTP 200 application/pdf. The 403 access-control endpoints are also verified server-side for a freshly-registered non-allowlisted user.
passed_tests: TestAccessControl: allowed login, list orders (both allowlisted emails), 403 for non-allowlisted user on list/create/catalog
TestCatalog: GET empty catalog, POST custom item persists, duplicate POST returns same id

TestPurchaseOrders: create increments PED-NNNN sequential, custom item auto-saved to supplier catalog on POST /purchase-orders, empty items rejected (400), status workflow pendente/enviado/recebido/reopen, invalid status rejected (400), PDF returns 200 application/pdf %PDF, delete removes from list

Frontend E2E: nav-pedidos visible for leonicelaboratorio@lumix.com, /pedidos page UI, new-order-dialog opens, supplier selection (real supplier), '+ adicionar item novo' adds to catalog, add to cart with quantity, cart qty edit, observations, Finalize creates PED-XXXX, status buttons (mark-sent, mark-received, reopen), PDF network call returns 200 application/pdf, navigator between Histórico and Pendentes/Entregues tabs
critical_code_review_comments: Allowlist comparison is case-insensitive (good) and centralised in require_pedidos_access().

Sequential PED-NNNN numbering uses a per-document 'seq' field with sort -1; safe under low concurrency, but two simultaneous POSTs could race. Consider db.purchase_orders.find_one_and_update on a counters collection if higher concurrency is expected.
_get_lumix_logo_path() caches the downloaded logo in /tmp; if download fails initially it returns None and PDF still renders (graceful).
Custom catalog items are auto-saved on order creation only when supplier_id is non-empty (avulso typed names are NOT saved to any catalog, which matches the spec).
delete_purchase_order does soft-delete only (sets deleted=True), as expected.
All endpoints exclude MongoDB _id via projection. Good.
Pedidos.js: all required data-testid attributes are present and behave as expected.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all critical flows passed; one non-essential re-open of dialog hit a click race, but the underlying flow was already verified)

seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_Fornecedor for backend tests; all test suppliers/orders/catalog items are cleaned up in teardown. Frontend test PED-0007 was created with 'Fornecedor Teste' and cleaned up post-run via API.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pedidos module is fully working backend + frontend. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_pedidos.py uses ALLOWED_EMAIL=laboratoriolumix@outlook.com / Lumix2002 and registers a random TEST user for 403 checks. The test cleans up its own data. To re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_pedidos.py -v. UI testids in Pedidos.js are stable and complete.
